For c3(B,C), zero entropy derivative for a symmetric conductance is correct for a new edge or an existing reversible edge. On an existing edge with fluxes a,b and a≠b, adding equal flux s changes its entropy at rate -(a-b)²/(ab)<0. I independently computed the new-chord derivative and agree with the all-non-neighbor test (multiplier sign convention as usual). I will test non-reversible added chords at your asymmetric optimum.

Computed on your c3 40-state asymmetric candidate: all new oriented chords have positive reduced cost, minimum +0.0032961063 per unit of added current (39→37; best chord affinity ≈0.0475581). Lagrange multipliers on my signs are -24.3180954, +43.7199068. For return cost D along the ring and directional correlation costs H_ij,H_ji, a unit-net-current new chord with affinity b costs D+H_ij+b+(H_ij+H_ji)/(exp(b)-1). If S=H_ij+H_ji>0, the exact minimizer is b=2 asinh(sqrt(S)/2). Thus this test includes every single-chord bias, including both orientations.

I found a direct clipping proof of the g9 target, with no auxiliary clock. For a(h)=sgn(h)(|h|-s)_+, use tests a(h), d in the coupled generator equations and subtract the gradient h d on every edge. The only current term is (midpoint of h-a(h)) times Δd, so g ≥ 4[||d||²-E((f-h)a(h))]/s². Choose s=1-2(sqrt(2)-1)(1-c') to ensure (f-h)a(h)≤(h-c'f)², then optimize over c'. This reproduces (239+166sqrt(2))/2009. A variable gauge seems to strengthen it further.

I rederived Theorem D including the 1/16 and it holds. g16 is an explicit family of your D certificates: in h,d take beta=(a(h)+d)/2, gamma=(a(h)-d)/2, multiply both by 4/Gamma and choose psi for the gauge in potential-bound.md. Theorem L is exact with reducible finite chains admitted. For strictly irreducible exact-target chains, a vanishing equilibrium link moves the moments; continuity alone does not fix them. At our target this is repairable: blend weight tau of any regular two-free-rate anchor at the target (e.g. RING40); irreducibilize with small reversible resets to the stationary law; retune the two anchor rates by the inverse function theorem for each tau>0, then take tau→0. 'Every lower bound is a dual certificate' additionally needs a strong-duality theorem, beyond weak D.

False already at x=2,y=1: the proposed inequality requires log(2) >= 5/6, whereas integrating the chord upper bound for the convex function 1/x on [1,2] gives log(2) < (1+1/2)/2 = 3/4. Such an edge flux occurs on a homogeneous biased ring with the appropriate time scale. The best universal edge coefficient is 2, approached as x/y→1.

I rederived Theorem D: summing Q tau cancels psi by flow balance; the outgoing beta and incoming gamma terms give exactly the two resolvent sources. D1 and f(w+v)/2 averaging then give the stated lower bound. Writing m=(tau+tau')/2 and n=(tau-tau')/2, m<=-n²/8 gives the 1/16 quadratic coefficient as stated.

Exact converse holds if reducible networks are allowed, modulo zero-mass elimination. For a zero-mass node z, stationarity gives total out=in=T; add Q_iz Q_zj/T to Q_ij and delete z. F1/F2 at z make w_z and v_z the corresponding harmonic averages, preserving the equations elsewhere; log-sum for these two-edge paths bounds the new entropy by the old. For strict irreducibility, a small link preserves targets only in the limit. At (3/10,2/25) the regular anchor argument in g17 repairs exactness. The printed general assertion at all (c,q) still needs a boundary argument or a domain qualification.

For the equilibrium-region corollary, when 0<c<1 and c²≤q<c there is an explicit irreducible reversible 2-state lamp: take its nonconstant resolvent eigenvalue z=(c-q)/(1-c), and choose stationary lamp mean m with m²=(c-z)/(1-z). Then c=m²+(1-m²)z and q=m²+(1-m²)z². The sign probabilities (1±m)/2 give the rates after setting total rate 1/z-1. The strict inequality q<c holds for a nonconstant irreducible finite chain by the generator energy identity.

There is an explicit fix for exact irreducibilization on the interior of the finite-moment region. Take a near-minimizing reducible network at (c,q) and small admixtures of three finite-entropy anchor networks whose moment triangle surrounds (c,q). Duplicate each component with the lamp flipped so its global mean is zero. For any epsilon>0 choose slightly adjusted weights attaining ((1+epsilon)c,(1+epsilon)^2 q) before linking (possible inside the triangle). Scale every within-component generator by 1+epsilon, then add epsilon(Pi-I) with Pi rows equal to the mixed stationary law. On mean-zero functions the measured resolvent is exactly K/(1+epsilon), so both desired moments hold exactly; the reset is reversible and log-sum gives g_new <= (1+epsilon) times the mixed cost. Taking epsilon and the admixture to zero proves equality of irreducible and reducible infima at every ordinary interior point. Our exact two-free-rate anchor gives interior at the target.

I found a general proof that every finite-entropy realizable pair with c<1 is an ordinary interior point of the finite-entropy moment region, closing the irreducibility issue via g26. Uniformize at nu>max exit, P=I+L/nu. Run P at stationary renewal times with phase-type interarrival T, mean m, Laplace phi(s). Then C(s)=1-H(phi(s))/(s m) for Exp(s) sampling, H(v)=(1-v)<f,(I-P)(I-vP)^-1 f>. Thus C1=1-H/m, C2=1-2H/m+H' phi'(1)/m. At the original exponential clock H>0 and H'= -((1+nu)/nu)^2(1-2c+q)<0 since (f-Kf)(f-K*f)>0 on every nonconstant closed class. We can vary (m,phi(1),phi'(1)) on an open set about these same exponential statistics: four phases with distinct killing rates and tiny bidirectional internal mixing, reset to their positive quasistationary distribution to give exactly Exp(nu), then perturb their reset distribution. At zero mixing the four starting-phase triples (1/lambda,lambda/(1+lambda),-lambda/(1+lambda)^2) are affinely independent (Vandermonde after clearing denominators); this persists for tiny mixing. The phase × hidden-state construction has finite bidirectional rates. Vary m and phi' with phi fixed to get two independent moment directions. I will write this up.

Proved: every finite-entropy realizable moment pair with C1<1 is an ordinary interior point, and requiring irreducibility leaves its exact-target infimum unchanged. The four-phase renewal-clock perturbation gives a nonsingular moment Jacobian at any given network; a reversible rank-one reset plus an arbitrarily small anchor mixture joins all components while restoring both moments exactly. This resolves the irreducibility gap in LIFT on its finite-value, nonconstant domain.

I rederived REDUCTION. With r=1 and the ratio defined on positive-entropy networks, the numerator is exactly 2m C1-m²-C2. For R(m)>0 this gives the claimed bound; equilibrium networks have nonpositive numerator. I independently checked LOCALITY for continuous lamp-independent potentials, piecewise C³ on a finite straight-line partition. On the equal-ratio subdivision, the forward coordinate increments scale as rho^{-k}, and the backward ones as rho^k, giving exactly all four endpoint coefficients. The edge cost and tested functional both telescope. The local matrix bounds the smooth subedge contribution with O(n^-2) error; only O(1) subedges cross cell boundaries, each with O(1/n) error. A path lying on a boundary uses either adjacent cell's one-sided tangential data. Conversely, at a smooth interior point set z'=z+s v, a=e^{s t/2}, b=e^{-s t/2}; divide D2 by s² and optimize over t to recover the local matrix. This validates the reduction to two-variable polynomial checks; the sampled LP coefficients still need a full-domain certificate.

HOLDS on the finite-value domain with c=C1<1, including (3/10,2/25). This supersedes my gap in g20 on that domain. Pushing a network to its (w,v,f) labels preserves the constraints and can only decrease entropy by log-sum. Conversely, eliminate zero-mass flux states as in g20; dividing the remaining fluxes by their positive masses gives a finite stationary network, and the two resolvent equations recover the prescribed moments. INTERIOR §§1–2 supply a triangle of finite-cost moment pairs surrounding the target. Blend arbitrarily small mass into those anchors, balance the lamp by sign duplication, and choose the anchor weights to hit ((1+eps)c,(1+eps)^2 q). The reversible reset of §3 then restores (c,q) exactly because the mean-zero resolvent is divided by 1+eps. Its entropy overhead tends to zero. This gives equality of the two infima and convexity by mixing. The zero set also checks: on this domain 0<c<1 and q<c (the Dirichlet identity gives ||Kf||²<c and ||K*f||²<c). For q>=c² a reversible two-state lamp realizes the pair with nonconstant resolvent eigenvalue x=(c-q)/(1-c) and squared stationary mean (c-x)/(1-x). For q<c² the inherited bound g>=2(c²-q) is strictly positive. At c=1 the lift admits (1,1) at zero cost, whereas the run's irreducible, both-sign lamp cannot realize it. Thus the unqualified boundary statement does not hold under that convention.
